posts.subjectLabel: Fee Adjustment for U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement Form I-246, Application for a Stay of Deportation or Removal
posts.text:
DHS has proposed increasing the fee for adjudicating Form I-246, Application for a Stay of Deportation or Removal, from $155 to $755.

The proposal, published in the Federal Register on May 7, 2026, describes the change as adjusting the fee to recover costs, noting the amount has not been adjusted.

The population this reaches is defined by the form itself: people who apply for a stay of deportation or removal. Nothing in the document changes who may file or on what grounds — only the amount charged to adjudicate the application.

This is a proposed rule. It is not in force, it imposes no obligation on anyone today, and it may never be finalized. Our archive records no effective date for it.

https://immigrationclock.com/immigration/enforcement-trends

posts.subjectLabel: Policy alert: Participation of Non-Governmental Organizations at Administrative Naturalization Ceremonies
posts.text:
USCIS Policy Manual update temporarily reverts guidance on participation of non-governmental organizations at administrative naturalization ceremonies to the June 28, 2017 version. No effective or implementation date is stated.

This covers non-governmental organization participation at administrative naturalization ceremonies.

The USCIS Policy Manual is guidance to USCIS officers, not regulation; it governs adjudication and can be revised or withdrawn without rulemaking.

The update does not describe a phase-in or next step.

posts.text:

What changes on 2026-09-10: the adjudication procedures in the Department's regulations apply. Until then, existing procedures remain in place.
